name: Alexander G. Flor
half: Alexander G. Flor has advised twenty theses in this repository between 2019 and 2024. Their most recent advisee graduated in 2024, with no new advisees recorded in 2026. Flor’s research interests span communication studies, climate and disaster management, arts and creative practice, culture and identity, gender and inclusion, management and leadership, governance and public policy, futures and philosophy, youth and family, and environment and sustainability. The advised works demonstrate a strong focus on communication studies, appearing in ten projects, followed by climate and disaster topics in six instances. Other frequent themes include arts and creative practice, culture and identity, gender and inclusion, management and leadership, governance and public policy, futures and philosophy, youth and family, and environment and sustainability. Recent supervised research includes investigations into religious communication needs and academic persistence among vocational students in Cebu City, human-animal interaction and mental wellness through autoethnography, and sports information seeking behaviors among persons with disabilities in the National Capital Region. Other projects examined family communication patterns among elementary students in Cavite, green coal acceptability in Bataan, and risk communication for coastal communities in Misamis Oriental. International supervision included a case study on organizational communication in Malang, Indonesia. Earlier theses addressed feminism in photography, TikTok’s role in political education for Overseas Filipino Workers in Qatar, and cyberage inequity in the Philippines. Flor also authored four items in the repository, including works on knowledge management for development, collective climate action, information and communication technology for development, and ASEAN identity discourses. These publications highlight their engagement with international development, open educational resources, and regional integration. The profile reflects a consistent advisory pattern in communication and development studies, with specific attention to marginalized groups, disaster resilience, and digital media impacts across various geographic contexts in Asia.

Alexander G. Flor has advised twenty theses in this repository between 2019 and 2024, with their latest item appearing in 2026, though they have no advisees recorded for that year. Their supervision record demonstrates a strong focus on communication studies, which appears in ten of the advised works. This primary interest intersects significantly with climate and disaster research, featured in six theses, and arts and creative practice, present in four. Other notable sub-topics include culture and identity, gender and inclusion, management and leadership, governance and public policy, futures and philosophy, youth and family, and environment and sustainability.

The advised theses reveal a pattern of examining communication dynamics within specific social, environmental, and institutional contexts. In 2024, Flor supervised work on religious communication needs and academic persistence among vocational students in Cebu City, as well as human-animal interaction and mental wellness through autoethnography. That same year, supervision extended to sports information seeking behavior among persons with disabilities in the National Capital Region and family communication patterns affecting child rights practices in Silang, Cavite. Environmental and sustainability concerns were addressed in a thesis on the social acceptability of green coal as an energy source in Bataan and another on risk communication and disaster preparedness for coastal communities in Misamis Oriental. International scope was evident in a 2024 case study on organizational communication and knowledge management at a senior high school in Malang, Indonesia.

Previous years show continued engagement with diverse topics. In 2023, supervised work included feminism in photography among Filipino photographers in Riyadh, the use of TikTok for political education among Overseas Filipino Workers in Qatar, and the influence of humanized communication on COVID-19 preventive measures in Quezon City. Research on cyberage inequity and technological access disparities was also supervised in 2023. The 2022 record includes a thesis on enhancing ASEAN’s immediate disaster management response, utilizing Super Typhoon Haiyan as a case study. Earlier years feature studies on risk communication validated through farmers’ responses to flood warnings in 2021, phenomenological narratives of journalists covering typhoons, and motivators for responsible pet ownership as a rabies preventive measure in Davao City. A 2021 dissertation also explored big data as a climate change intervention.

In 2020, Flor supervised research on the changes in communication patterns and lifestyles of the Sama-Bajau community in Cabanatuan City, the liberating potential of social media in the Philippine context, and the theoretical link between instruction and communication. The 2019 record includes a thesis on information and communication technology access among people with disabilities. Beyond advising, Flor has authored or edited four own articles in this repository, all published in 2019. These works cover knowledge management for development, collective climate action, information and communication technology for development, and ASEAN convergence regarding identity, communication, and culture. The profile indicates a consistent scholarly interest in the intersection of communication, development, and societal challenges, with supervision spanning from local community issues in the Philippines to regional cooperation in ASEAN and international development contexts.

The adviser demonstrates a strong engagement with climate and disaster communication, a topic featured in six items.
